featured_reviews.review_text:

Overall it was a good experience and definitely calls for a second visit for cheesecake

I ordered an Arrabbiata pasta and asked them to replace mushroom with another vegetable. That’s it. Not extra toppings, not some complicated off-menu request — just replacing one vegetable.

And honestly, calling that a “special customization” is ridiculous. It’s pasta, not a five-course tasting menu. Also, I have genuinely never seen mushroom in an Arrabbiata pasta on any normal menu, so acting like removing it was some massive inconvenience was bizarre from the start.

The pasta arrived completely dry, non-palatable, and barely edible, so I gave it 2 stars on the app. I didn’t even write a review initially. But apparently that was enough to trigger the owner into calling me at 11 PM to argue about why I gave a low rating.

The entire call was just constant interruption, defensiveness, and repeated lectures about how they had gone “out of their way” for me by replacing one vegetable with another. If that is considered some massive favour, then maybe don’t offer it at all.

What’s worse is the complete inability to take feedback. If you ask a customer what went wrong, at least let them speak instead of interrupting them every few seconds.

In the restaurant business, bad food is still fixable. This kind of behaviour is what actually ruins the experience. Calling customers late at night to fight over a rating is genuinely bizarre and unbelievably unprofessional.

Definitely not ordering again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited August Café recently and came away with mixed feelings.

We ordered the Mushroom Sandwich on sourdough, Paneer Tikka Panini, Pink Sauce Pasta, Veg Burger with fries, Cold Chocolate, and ended the meal with a Chocolate Cake.

Starting with the sandwiches, the Mushroom Sandwich was unfortunately quite dry and lacked the moisture and flavour you would expect. The Paneer Tikka Panini had the opposite problem, the mustard was so overpowering that it completely dominated the dish, making it taste more like a mustard sandwich than a paneer tikka panini.

The Pink Sauce Pasta was decent but nothing memorable. It wasn't bad, but it didn't stand out either.

The Veg Burger was actually the star of the meal. It was well-made, flavourful, and easily the best savoury dish we ordered. However, what left a sour taste was being charged ₹50 extra to make just a handful of fries peri-peri. Charging that amount for a full portion is understandable, but for barely six fries on the side, it felt excessive and unnecessary.

The Cold Chocolate was another disappointment—not because of the taste, which was perfectly fine, but because of the quantity. The portion felt quite small for the price being charged.

Thankfully, dessert ended the meal on a positive note. The Chocolate Cake was rich, delicious, and probably the highlight of the entire experience.

Overall, August Café has a pleasant atmosphere and some good offerings, but the food lacked consistency and some of the pricing decisions felt difficult to justify. Not a bad experience, but not one that left a strong impression either.

⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited August Café recently and had quite a mixed but overall pleasant experience.

Starting with the Pho, this unfortunately missed the mark. It wasn’t authentic, used the wrong type of noodles, and the balance of flavours was overwhelmed by an excess of chilli oil and flakes. The Soy Chilli Noodles were also underwhelming; they lacked depth and flavour, and didn’t really stand out as a noodle dish.

On the brighter side, the Nachos were, as always, spot on, crisp, generously topped, and satisfying. The Chicken Steak with Peri Peri Sauce was another highlight, perfectly cooked, tender, and flavourful, paired beautifully with fresh, well-seasoned vegetables.

For drinks, the Elderberry Fizz with soda and basil seeds was refreshing and unique, while the Cappuccino was smooth and well-prepared.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to this spot on Saturday morning for breakfast, and it turned out to be a fantastic experience for us.

We ordered one Cortado, a large Pain au Chocolat, a spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown, an avocado chicken sandwich, and a Caramel Latte.

The cortado was incredible; it's a traditional Spanish espresso drink made with double espresso and 60 ml of milk. It had a bitter flavour, but I really enjoyed it.

The large pain au chocolat was absolutely delicious, a classic pastry crafted from buttery, flaky, laminated dough (similar to croissant dough) wrapped around dark chocolate sticks.

The spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown was tasty, featuring shredded potatoes filled with cooked chicken, pan-fried until golden and crispy.The avocado chicken sandwich was mouthwatering and highly recommended. It was a fresh, nutritious, and versatile meal made with thin slices of chicken and avocado. Simply delightful.

The caramel latte was incredibly refreshing. It’s a sweet and creamy coffee drink typically made with espresso, steamed milk, and caramel syrup.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great experience at Boojee Cafe. Absolutely loved how this cafe is designed-it may look small from the outside, but the interiors are planned so well that it feels surprisingly spacious and comfortable once you step in. It’s a perfect spot for a quick bite with friends or even a casual catch-up over coffee.

The place gets quite packed on weekends. We went on a Saturday and had to wait around 5–10 minutes for a table, which honestly just shows how popular the cafe is.

The food and coffee here are fantastic. The House Cold Coffee was suggested to us and it truly lived up to the hype, a must-try if you’re a genuine coffee lover. We also tried the Orange Cold Brew. Personally, I didn’t enjoy it as much, but it definitely feels like an acquired taste, so cold brew enthusiasts should still give it a shot.

For food, we tried the Chicken & Veggies Mini Wrap and it was amazing, especially the dip served alongside it which paired perfectly with the wrap.

Another big plus point was the staff and service. The staff is friendly, welcoming and the service is impressively quick despite the crowd.

Overall, a really nice cafe with great vibes, good food and excellent coffee. Would definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in and around Bandra.

We had the Muttuswamy Special Benne Dosa, which is a mix of Benne Dosa, Masala Dosa and Ghee Podi Dosa. We also had Idli Vada Rasam, Plain and Hazelnut Filter Coffee, and a Pineapple Sheera to top it off. All of it was delicious, as well as pleasing to the eye!

The restaurant has been done up beautifully - it feels like you're walking into another world. It's super clean, and all the little touches - from the dabbara set for the filter coffee, to the paan box for the mukhwaas - serve to further elevate the experience.

Special thanks to Gaurav for being so patient and helpful.

I only dock one star because the AC wasn't working, and it's upwards of 35 degrees C right now. But honestly, the food was worth it.

10/10, would recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka
featured_reviews.review_text:
### **Review for Prithvi Café**
Prithvi Café is legendary for its vibe and history, but if I’m being honest, the food felt a bit overhyped. It’s a great spot to hang out, but the flavors were a hit-or-miss for me :(

So, I was leaving for out of India but just wanted to explore this cafe before leaving as I will be missing Indian food a little!
But, I kind of got disappointed with the food. To be honest the dishes I had at airport were better🥲

**The Food Breakdown:**
🌟 Egg Kheema: Just okay. It didn't quite live up to the expectations I had based on the reviews.
🌟 Butter Chicken Thali: This was a letdown. The gravy was **way too sweet**—even for Butter Chicken. It lacked that savory, spicy balance you'd expect.
🌟 Mixed Veg Paratha: One of the better items we ordered. Solid, filling, and tasted fresh.
🌟 Burger (Must Try!): The highlight of the meal. The bun isn't made of maida (refined flour), which gave it a great texture. Definitely worth a try if you want something "healthier" but tasty.
Chocolate Croissant: A decent sweet finish, but nothing groundbreaking.

**Drinks:**
We tried the Blueberry Soda and Masala Soda. Both were refreshing and served as good palate cleansers for the meal.

Go for the atmosphere and the non-maida burgers, but maybe skip the North Indian mains if you aren't a fan of sweet gravies. It's a nice place to chill, just don't expect a culinary masterpiece across the whole menu.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text: Inspite of visiting a couple of times before, we've never shot pictures to upload in the review as this was a busy place that involved queue system to be seated. Our last visit was on a weekday afternoon and hence we got a table without a wait time. The seating is outdoor and the menu is pocket friendly and extensive. Most of their kitchen seems outdoor and causes fumes,sizzles and fragrances of multiple dishes being cooked. The dining is moderately under dhaded trees and thoroughly placed table fans. The menu and ordering are online while the bill can be paid once your are  about to leave. Service staff are busy but give you attention when needed. Our asked for extra plate/spoon have immediately been fulfilled. The orders once placed have also arrived quick to the table. We've been ordering from this place for years and hence have reordered most of our favorites to enjoy them fresh which include their paratha with dal makhani, red velvet brownie and cookies. Their sulemani chai and masala soda were well made too. No excessive sugars in the beverages that we ordered. Overall it was a nostalgic place for us and being able to dine without a wait time is a plus.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited **Prithvi Café** and had a really good experience overall. The café has a beautiful, lively ambience with a chilled, artsy vibe — perfect for casual meetups or relaxed meals.

I tried quite a few dishes here:
🍽️ **Amritsari Paratha** – Nicely stuffed, flavorful, and served hot with curd and chutney. The taste was authentic and had a pleasant spicy punch without being overpowering.
🍝 **White Pasta** – Creamy, rich, and perfectly cooked. The sauce was smooth and mildly cheesy, though it could use a little more spice for those who like stronger flavors.
☕ **Hot Coffee & Filter Coffee Ice-Cream** – Both were excellent. The hot coffee was strong and aromatic, while the filter coffee ice-cream was a unique treat — a perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness.
🥭 **Mango Lassi** – Thick, fresh, and refreshing, with a real mango flavor. It paired well with the paratha and gave a nice desi touch to the meal.
🌯 **Chicken Roll** – Juicy, well-marinated, and wrapped in soft bread. Nicely spiced and filling; non-veg lovers will definitely enjoy this.

The **service** was polite and quick despite the crowd. **Pricing** is slightly on the higher side, but the taste and ambience justify it. The **outdoor seating** under trees gives a cozy, café-theatre vibe that’s hard to find elsewhere in Mumbai.

✅ **Overall:** Quite good experience — tasty food, soothing coffee, and vibrant atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re near Juhu, especially for coffee lovers and café enthusiasts
